content.text:
Here is the complete revised research proposal as a JSON object, addressing all 7 reviewer issues with a **major revision**:

```json
{
  "title": "Beyond Step-Local Verification: Tracing Perception Error Cascades in Multimodal Process Reward Models",
  "change_type": "major",
  "core_problem": "Multimodal process reward models verify each reasoning step independently, missing cascade errors: steps where local reasoning is valid but produces wrong results because upstream visual information was misperceived. When a VLM misreads '45 degrees' as '90 degrees' in step 2, steps 3-7 may apply flawless trigonometry to the wrong angle -- appearing locally correct but systematically producing wrong answers. Cascade errors are invisible to binary correct/incorrect labels, to simple perception/reasoning classification (the cascade step's own reasoning IS correct), and even to Perceval's hallucination detection (no hallucination occurs at the cascade step itself). Across 4+ independent studies, 67-87% of VLM errors originate from visual perception, and each perception error can corrupt multiple downstream steps. The current VisualProcessBench SOTA (EVPV-PRM at 67.46 F1, Athena-PRM at 65.9 F1) evaluates each step independently -- no existing verification method detects cascade errors. EVPV explicitly flags step-local cascade tracking as future work; MMErroR explicitly excludes cascading errors from evaluation; PARC models accumulation errors but only in text-only settings; Proof-of-Perception uses DAGs with conformal prediction for inference-time certification but not for training-time error labeling. Cascade-aware verification requires a fundamentally new capability: dependency-aware step evaluation that traces visual information flow through reasoning chains.",
  "opportunity": "Four converging developments make cascade-aware multimodal PRMs both timely and feasible. (1) The cascade detection gap is now explicitly acknowledged and remains unfilled despite rapid SOTA progress. EVPV/Grounding the Score (March 2026) achieves 67.46 F1 on VisualProcessBench using global reliability signals for visual premise verification but states that 'step-local reliability is an important next step' -- precisely our contribution. Athena-PRM (June 2026) achieves 65.9 F1 via data-efficient training with weak-strong completer filtering, but remains step-independent with binary labels. MMErroR (Jan 2026) explicitly excludes cascading errors from their benchmark. Hallucination propagation research (arXiv 2603.27201) empirically shows that cascade errors produce 'locally plausible, internally coherent' steps that mask underlying errors. The SOTA has improved rapidly (62.0 -> 65.9 -> 67.46 F1 on VisualProcessBench) through better data quality and visual grounding, but all improvements are within the step-independent paradigm -- the cascade detection gap persists. (2) Text-only cascade detection proves the concept. PARC (Feb 2025) models 'accumulation errors' via premise-augmented DAGs in text-only reasoning, distinguishing root-cause from propagated errors. CRM (2025) captures causal relationships among reasoning steps. ReasonDiag (March 2026) finds ~44.5% of verification false positives stem from error propagation. These demonstrate that dependency-aware verification is valuable -- extending it to the multimodal perception-reasoning boundary is the natural next step. (3) DAG-based reasoning structures have been validated for multimodal settings. Proof-of-Perception (Feb 2026) models multimodal reasoning as executable DAGs with conformal prediction at each node, reducing error compounding during inference. This validates the structural premise -- reasoning as a DAG with typed nodes -- while targeting a different goal (inference-time certification vs. our training-time cascade labeling). Controllable Process Data Synthesis (May 2026) demonstrates that downstream-propagated errors can be distinguished from source errors via symbolic recomputation. (4) Perception-aware RL methods have matured but plateau at step-independent decomposition. PDCR (May 2026) uses unsupervised Visual Dependence Scores to separate perception and reasoning rewards via skill clustering, achieving 76.2% step classification accuracy -- but processes each step independently within its skill cluster without modeling cross-step cascades. The missing capability across all approaches is dependency-aware verification -- and the multimodal setting creates the strongest need for it.",
  "landscape": "The landscape segments into five clusters, none occupying CascadePRM's position at the intersection of multimodal perception-awareness and dependency-aware verification.

**Cluster A -- Step-Independent Multimodal PRMs.** Training VL-PRMs (arXiv 2509.23250) provides VL-PRM300K (1.32M steps) with binary labels despite noting 86% perception errors. VisualPRM (arXiv 2503.10291) provides VisualProcessBench (26,950 human labels), binary only. Athena-PRM (arXiv 2506.09532) achieves 65.9 F1 on VisualProcessBench via data-efficient weak-strong completer filtering with only 5K samples, with ORM initialization and negative up-sampling -- current data-efficiency SOTA but still binary step-independent. DreamPRM-1.5, TIM-PRM (61.7 F1), VRPRM, MM-PRM, URSA all produce binary step scores. All evaluate each step independently without modeling cross-step information flow.

**Cluster B -- Perception-Aware Step-Independent Verification.** Perceval (arXiv 2604.24583, April 2026) detects hallucinated spans via token-level binary classification -- closest existing work on perception-aware PRM, but treats each step independently and cannot distinguish cascade errors from direct errors. GM-PRM (arXiv 2508.04088) evaluates {step intent, visual alignment, reasoning logic} as structured CoT for generative scoring, but evaluations are step-independent with no cross-step dependency modeling. EVPV/Grounding the Score (arXiv 2603.16253) achieves 67.46 F1 on VisualProcessBench -- current overall SOTA -- via visual reliability gating with checklist verification, but uses candidate-level (global) rather than step-local reliability, and explicitly identifies step-local cascade tracking as future work. Proof-of-Perception (arXiv 2603.00324) models multimodal reasoning as executable DAGs with conformal prediction at each node, reducing error compounding during inference via set-valued predictions and a budget-aware controller -- the closest structural analog to our DAG approach, but targets inference-time certification with statistical guarantees rather than training-time cascade label generation for PRM training.

**Cluster C -- Perception-Aware RL Optimization (Downstream).** PAPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2507.06448) uses implicit perception loss via masked-image KL divergence in GRPO. VPPO (ICLR 2026, arXiv 2510.09285) reweights by visual dependency tokens. PDCR (arXiv 2605.13467, May 2026) decomposes perception and reasoning rewards via unsupervised skill clustering with a Visual Dependence Score (VDS), applying Otsu's method to separate perception-heavy from reasoning-heavy steps and normalizing confidence gains within each cluster -- the most sophisticated perception-reasoning credit decomposition at the RL level, achieving 76.2% step classification accuracy, but processes each step independently within its skill cluster without modeling cross-step cascades. AT-RL (arXiv 2602.11455), PRCO (arXiv 2603.28618), Perception-R1 (ICLR 2026), and 'Bad Seeing or Bad Thinking' (ICML 2026 Spotlight) all operate at RL reward/policy level. These consume PRM outputs as scalar rewards; cascade-aware PRM outputs would directly improve the quality of signals these methods consume.

**Cluster D -- Text-Only Dependency-Aware Verification.** PARC (arXiv 2502.02362) introduces 'accumulation errors' via premise-augmented DAGs, distinguishing root-cause from propagated errors -- the closest text-only analog to cascade detection, but no multimodal component. CRM (arXiv 2509.26578) captures causal relationships among text reasoning steps via conditional probability chains. ReasonDiag (arXiv 2603.21286) visualizes error propagation patterns in text-only CoT, finding ~44.5% of verification false positives from error propagation. RewardFlow (arXiv 2603.18859) uses topology-aware propagation in state graphs. All are text-only and do not address the perception-reasoning boundary.

**Cluster E -- Error Taxonomies Without Cascade Detection.** PathFinder-PRM (arXiv 2505.19706) uses {math, consistency} types in text-only PRMs; ablation shows category separation contributes only -0.4 vs -2.8 for hierarchical structure, motivating dependency-aware hierarchy over flat type labels. ErrorRadar (ICLR 2025 Workshop) provides multimodal error types for benchmarking, not PRM training. MMErroR (arXiv 2601.03331) defines error types but explicitly states each sample contains a single coherent error, excluding cascading errors. ThinkWithImages-PRMBench (arXiv 2602.08346) defines 7 error types across 4 categories -- none is a cascade error.

**CascadePRM's unique position**: We bridge Cluster B (multimodal perception-aware verification) with Cluster D (dependency-aware verification) to detect cascade errors -- the gap explicitly acknowledged by EVPV, excluded by MMErroR, structurally enabled but not targeted by Proof-of-Perception, and unaddressed by any existing multimodal PRM including the current SOTA (EVPV-PRM at 67.46 F1, Athena-PRM at 65.9 F1).",
  "inspired_by": "Four conceptual bridges define CascadePRM's contribution. (1) PARC's accumulation error framework proves that distinguishing root-cause from propagated errors improves text-only verification, but the perception-reasoning boundary in multimodal settings creates a far more impactful instance: upstream perception failures cascade through downstream reasoning in ways that are mechanistically distinct from text-only logical propagation, because the root cause is cross-modal (visual processing failure) while the cascade is within-modal (text reasoning). (2) EVPV's explicit limitation creates our opportunity: their global reliability signal attenuates all steps uniformly when visual reliability is low, but cascade errors require step-local analysis -- a step that doesn't reference the image at all can still be a cascade error if it uses a value derived from an earlier misperception. The EVPV authors themselves identify step-local reliability as the 'important next step.' (3) Proof-of-Perception validates the structural premise of modeling multimodal reasoning as DAGs, but applies conformal prediction for inference-time reliability rather than generating training labels. We adopt the DAG structure for a complementary purpose: tracing visual information flow to generate cascade labels for PRM training. Where Proof-of-Perception asks 'is this node's output reliable enough to proceed?' we ask 'is this step wrong because of its own error, or because of an upstream perception error?' (4) PathFinder-PRM's ablation reveals that hierarchical structure (error detection guiding reward prediction) matters more than error type labels alone (-2.8 vs -0.4 on PRMBench). This shapes our approach: rather than simply classifying error types, we build a dependency-aware hierarchy where cascade detection provides richer structural information than flat type classification. The counterfactual formalization -- 'would this step be correct if the upstream perception were corrected?' -- provides an objective, testable definition of cascade errors. Recent work on LLM counterfactual reasoning (Executable Counterfactuals, ICLR 2026; Flying Pigs/FaR, 2025) shows a 14-40% accuracy drop for open-ended counterfactual reasoning, but our counterfactual task is far more constrained: it asks about mathematical value substitution in a single step, which we validate via a dedicated pilot study.",
  "approach": "We propose CascadePRM, a framework for detecting and leveraging perception error cascades in multimodal reasoning verification, comprising five components: (0) pilot validation studies, (1) a counterfactual cascade detection algorithm, (2) a cascade-annotated benchmark and dataset, (3) cascade-aware PRM training, and (4) downstream integration.

**Component 0: Pilot Validation Studies (Weeks 1-2, Gate for Subsequent Components).**

Two pilot studies validate the highest-risk pipeline components before committing to full-scale execution.

(Pilot A) Counterfactual Verification Reliability (50-100 samples, week 1): Select 50-100 incorrect steps from VisualProcessBench where the root-cause perception error is unambiguous (expert-identified). For each downstream dependent step, construct the counterfactual prompt and test whether Qwen2.5-VL-72B, InternVL2.5-78B, and Gemini-2.5-Flash can reliably answer 'would this step be correct if [quantity] were [correct_value] instead of [misperceived_value]?' We measure: (i) individual VLM accuracy on counterfactual verification (target: >75% per VLM); (ii) ensemble majority-vote accuracy (target: >85%); (iii) breakdown by problem type (geometry/chart/table) and counterfactual complexity (single value substitution vs. multi-value). This is the single highest-risk component: if ensemble accuracy is <70%, we redesign counterfactual verification using symbolic re-execution (see Contingency A below). Crucially, our counterfactual task is more constrained than the open-ended counterfactual reasoning benchmarked in prior work (Executable Counterfactuals, ICLR 2026, shows 25-40% accuracy drops): we provide the specific corrected value and ask about a single step's mathematical validity, reducing the task to localized arithmetic checking rather than open-ended hypothetical reasoning.

(Pilot B) Cascade Annotation Feasibility (200 steps, weeks 1-2): Three annotators independently annotate 200 incorrect steps from VisualProcessBench with full cascade labels: (i) visual claim identification per step, (ii) dependency graph edges, (iii) 3-tier error type {perception, reasoning, cascade} with root-cause provenance for cascade errors. We measure: (i) per-step annotation time (estimated 3-5 minutes for cascade tracing vs. <1 minute for binary labels; if >7 minutes, simplify the annotation protocol); (ii) inter-annotator kappa at each granularity level; (iii) annotator fatigue curve (agreement in first 50 vs. last 50 steps). If 3-tier kappa < 0.55 (below moderate agreement), we fall back to the binary {root-cause vs. cascade} taxonomy with the counterfactual criterion, which should achieve kappa > 0.70. This pilot gates the full annotation effort (Component 2).

**Component 1: Counterfactual Cascade Detection Algorithm (Primary Novelty, Weeks 2-7).**

We formalize cascade errors and build an automated detection pipeline in four stages, with per-stage accuracy estimates and a multiplicative error propagation analysis.

(Stage 1) Visual Claim Extraction: For each step in a solution, extract all claims that reference information derived from the image (e.g., 'angle ABC = 45 deg', 'the bar for 2020 shows 3.2M'). Uses Qwen2.5-VL-72B with targeted prompts. *Estimated accuracy: 88-92%.* Visual claims are relatively concrete and extractable; EVPV's visual checklist verification demonstrates that VLMs can reliably identify visual premises in reasoning steps. Errors at this stage produce false negatives (missed cascade labels) rather than false positives, because uncaptured visual claims simply won't be traced downstream.

(Stage 2) Information Flow Graph Construction: Build a directed acyclic graph (DAG) where nodes are reasoning steps and edges connect step j to step k if step k uses a quantity, relationship, or fact derived from visual claims in step j (directly or transitively). This extends PARC's premise-augmented DAG framework from text-only logical dependencies to cross-modal visual-to-reasoning dependencies. Unlike Proof-of-Perception's DAGs (which are generated via a domain-specific language for inference-time tool orchestration), our DAGs trace information flow through natural language reasoning chains for training-time label generation. *Estimated accuracy: 82-88%.* DAG construction requires identifying value dependencies across steps, which is more challenging than claim extraction but benefits from the structured nature of mathematical reasoning (values are explicitly referenced). Errors at this stage can produce both false positives (spurious edges causing over-labeling of cascade errors) and false negatives (missing edges causing under-labeling).

(Stage 3) Perception Error Identification: For each step containing visual claims, verify claims against the image using ensemble VLM voting (Qwen2.5-VL-72B, InternVL2.5-78B, Gemini-2.5-Flash). Steps with incorrect visual claims verified by majority vote are labeled as root-cause perception errors. *Estimated accuracy: 83-88%.* Ensemble voting provides robustness; PDCR's Visual Dependence Score achieves 76.2% on a related but harder task (unsupervised classification without explicit verification). Our dedicated verification with focused prompts should exceed this.

(Stage 4) Counterfactual Cascade Verification: For each downstream step k depending (via the DAG) on a root-cause perception error at step j: (a) extract the misperceived value and determine the correct value; (b) construct a counterfactual prompt: 'Given that [quantity] is actually [correct_value] rather than [misperceived_value], is the reasoning in step k valid?'; (c) if reasoning IS locally valid (confirmed by 2/3 VLMs), label step k as CASCADE; (d) if NOT locally valid, label as direct error. *Estimated accuracy: 80-87% (validated by Pilot A; target >85% ensemble).*

**Pipeline Error Propagation Analysis:** Under a worst-case multiplicative model assuming fully independent stages, end-to-end cascade detection accuracy = 0.88 x 0.82 x 0.83 x 0.80 = ~47.9%. However, this dramatically overstates actual error because: (a) Stage errors are NOT independent -- a step with clearly extracted visual claims (Stage 1 success) is also easier for DAG construction (Stage 2) and perception verification (Stage 3). (b) Different stage failure modes affect cascade labels differently: Stage 1 false negatives produce missed cascade labels (lower recall) but not wrong labels (preserving precision); Stage 2 false positive edges can be caught by Stage 4 (the counterfactual test rejects cascade labels where reasoning is independently wrong). (c) Confidence calibration filters out low-confidence cases: at 3/3 VLM agreement (~70-75% of cases), per-stage accuracy rises to 90-95%, yielding end-to-end accuracy of ~66-81% on the high-confidence subset.

We model three tiers: HIGH confidence (3/3 agreement across all stages, ~50-55% of cascade candidates): estimated >80% end-to-end accuracy, used with full label weight. MEDIUM confidence (2/3 at any stage, ~25-30%): estimated 55-70% accuracy, used with reduced weight (0.5). LOW confidence (~15-20%): routed to human review. We pre-commit to reporting: (i) per-stage accuracy on the pilot set; (ii) end-to-end cascade detection precision, recall, F1 on the gold benchmark; (iii) accuracy stratified by confidence tier. **Target: >75% cascade detection F1 on the gold benchmark (revised down from 80% based on pipeline analysis), with >85% precision on high-confidence subset.**

**Contingency A (Counterfactual Verification Failure):** If Pilot A shows ensemble counterfactual accuracy <70%, we replace Stage 4 with symbolic re-execution: for mathematical steps, extract the computation symbolically, substitute the corrected value, and check whether the output matches. This follows the methodology validated by Controllable Process Data Synthesis (arXiv 2605.02395). Symbolic re-execution is more limited (works for explicit calculations, not qualitative reasoning) but more reliable. We estimate this covers ~60-70% of cascade steps (those involving explicit mathematical operations), with VLM counterfactual verification retained for the remainder.

**Component 2: Cascade-Annotated Benchmark and Dataset (Weeks 2-8).**

(Phase A) Gold-Standard Benchmark -- VisualProcessBench-Cascade: Extend VisualProcessBench's 2,866 samples (~8,000 incorrect steps) with cascade annotations, gated by Pilot B results. For each incorrect step, annotators (6 graduate-level, STEM backgrounds, trained via the 200-step pilot protocol) assign: (i) a 3-tier error type {perception, reasoning, cascade} as the core taxonomy; (ii) an optional fine-grained subtype for non-cascade errors; (iii) for cascade errors: the root-cause step ID and the misperceived value. Target inter-annotator agreement: Cohen's kappa > 0.65 for 3-tier classification. Annotation protocol includes: mandatory 15-minute breaks every 90 minutes; daily calibration sessions on 10 shared examples; annotation batches of 50 steps maximum to mitigate fatigue. Estimated per-step time: 3-5 minutes (from Pilot B), yielding ~400-670 annotator-hours for 8,000 steps.

Pre-committed granularity fallback: If 3-tier kappa falls below 0.60, we report the {root-cause error vs. cascade error} binary taxonomy, which should achieve kappa > 0.70 as a binary classification with an objective counterfactual criterion.

(Phase B) Large-Scale Dataset -- VL-PRM-Cascade: Apply the automated cascade detection pipeline (Component 1) to VL-PRM300K (1.32M steps). Three-tier confidence calibration. Validate against gold benchmark.

**Component 3: Cascade-Aware PRM Training (Weeks 7-12).**

Train multimodal PRMs (InternVL2.5-8B backbone) with five training regimes forming a granularity ladder:

(A) Binary baseline: standard correct/incorrect on VL-PRM300K.
(B) 2-way typed: {perception error, reasoning error}.
(C) 3-way cascade-aware (PRIMARY MODEL): {perception, reasoning, cascade} with a two-stage prediction architecture: first predict error type, then predict correctness conditioned on error type. For cascade errors, the model additionally predicts the root-cause step.
(D) 3-way with cascade-weighted loss: same taxonomy as (C) but with cascade-specific loss weighting. w(cascade) > w(perception) > w(reasoning).
(E) Full fine-grained (ablation): complete sub-category decomposition.

Compare against current SOTA baselines: (i) Athena-PRM (65.9 F1 on VisualProcessBench, binary, data-efficient); (ii) EVPV-PRM (67.46 F1, global reliability gating); (iii) Perceval (binary hallucination PRM); (iv) GM-PRM (dimensional CoT).

**Component 4: Downstream Integration -- EVPV Enhancement (Weeks 10-13).**

(Integration A) Replace EVPV's global reliability signal with CascadePRM's step-local cascade scores. Steps with no visual dependency path are scored at full weight regardless of global reliability.

(Integration B) Cascade-aware advantage weighting for RL: following DRM's multi-dimensional GRPO framework, provide separate advantage signals for perception-error steps and cascade steps.

**Phase 5: Evaluation and Ablations (Weeks 10-15).**

Evaluate on: (a) VisualProcessBench-Cascade: step-level F1 for binary correctness, 3-way error type classification, and cascade detection accuracy; (b) downstream Best-of-N reranking on MathVista, MathVision, WeMath, ChartQA, PuzzleVQA with N=8,16,64; (c) EVPV integration: step-local vs. global reliability; (d) cascade-specific analysis stratified by cascade depth, visual modality, and cascade frequency.

Key ablations: (i) granularity ladder; (ii) counterfactual verification vs. simple dependency-based labeling vs. symbolic re-execution; (iii) cascade-weighted vs. uniform loss; (iv) head-to-head vs. Athena-PRM and EVPV-PRM on cascade-heavy problems; (v) high-confidence-only vs. all labels vs. human-verified; (vi) CascadePRM + EVPV vs. EVPV alone.

**Expected Results -- Calibrated Against Current SOTA.** The VisualProcessBench SOTA is EVPV-PRM at 67.46 F1. Athena-PRM achieves 65.9 F1. We predict: (1) CascadePRM achieves 69.5-71.5 F1 on VisualProcessBench (+2-4 over EVPV-PRM), with the primary gains from correct handling of cascade steps. (2) On cascade-heavy subsets (geometry, diagram problems), disproportionately larger gains (+4-7). (3) The granularity ladder's largest marginal improvement comes at {perception, reasoning} -> {perception, reasoning, cascade}. (4) Best-of-N reranking: +1-2 on MathVista, +2-3 on WeMath. (5) EVPV integration: +0.5-1.5 over EVPV alone. Conservative scenario: even +1.5 on VisualProcessBench over EVPV-PRM is publishable alongside the first empirical characterization of cascade errors and released artifacts.",
```
